# kit-implement

Resolve the requested behavior and inspect existing patterns. Use the project instructions and only relevant skills. Implement small tasks directly; for complex work identify acceptance criteria and dependencies before editing.

## Entry modes

- Default (`/cook`): implement the requested feature. If the user supplies an existing plan, use it.
- `--from-plan` (`/code`): locate the supplied or clearly active plan, read the overview first, validate its assumptions/dependencies and load one phase at a time as execution reaches it. Resume the next pending phase, verify it and update its status before proceeding. If no plan is identifiable, obtain the missing plan or prepare one within the user's scope rather than inventing its contents.
- `--bootstrap`: initialize the requested new project with the selected stack. Inspect the target first; preserve existing files, choose only required dependencies and verify the initial application can run/build. Do not scaffold over an existing project blindly. Explain stack choices where not already selected, apply relevant design conventions, create needed initial project docs and provide runnable getting-started/environment instructions.
- `--auto`: create or reuse a persisted implementation overview and phase files before executing them, including for small automatic tasks. With `--fast`, use local-only fast planning; otherwise research material uncertainties proportionally. Then proceed through authorized reversible stages without repeated approval. This does not expand permission to deploy, publish, push or message.
- `--fast`: reduce ceremony for a well-understood task; retain necessary verification and review.

## Delivery and plan progress

Make the smallest complete change. Run the relevant tests, type checks and build checks, inspect failures, and review the diff. Do not claim success from placeholder commands or skipped checks.

When following a plan, update its phase checkboxes and overview status only after the associated acceptance criteria pass. Keep incomplete or blocked work visible, with concrete evidence. A read-only reviewer reports proposed status corrections; the coordinator or project-manager writes them. Update affected existing documentation, roadmap and changelog when the change warrants it, without creating unrelated files. Hand off changed paths, checks, plan progress and remaining risks.

Preserve existing API contracts and backward compatibility. Identify and document intentional breaking changes and their migration steps rather than silently changing consumers.
